themes_detail.label: Rodent infestation surge
themes_detail.summary: Rodent complaints spiked to 8 this week compared to a baseline average of 1.2 per week over the prior 8 weeks—a 540% increase with a z-score of 6.19—signaling a potential widespread infestation outbreak in Queens Village/Cambria Heights.
evidence: 8 rodent complaints THIS WEEK vs. 1.2 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (540% spike, z-score 6.19)
Highest statistical anomaly in dataset; spike meets severity threshold for epidemic-level pattern
Complaint volume suggests multiple affected locations, not isolated incidents
reporting_angles: Interview residents across the district to map where infestations are occurring and identify common triggers (trash collection delays, construction, food sources)
Contact NYC Health Department and Department of Sanitation to learn if they've detected a pattern and what response is underway

themes_detail.label: Unleashed dogs spike
themes_detail.summary: Unleashed dog complaints jumped to 5 this week versus a baseline of 0.8 per week—a 567% spike (z-score 4.39)—raising public safety concerns in parks and streets.
evidence: 5 unleashed dog complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.8 weekly average (567% increase, z-score 4.39)
Spike aligns with warmer weather when residents use parks more frequently
Second-highest z-score in dataset; indicates acute emergence of issue
reporting_angles: Interview park users and residents about specific locations where unleashed dogs pose risks to children and other pets
Check with Parks Department and local precinct about enforcement patterns and whether leash law education is being prioritized

themes_detail.label: Illegal tree damage escalation
themes_detail.summary: Illegal tree damage complaints reached 4 this week compared to 0.8 per week baseline—a 433% spike (z-score 4.91)—suggesting either construction activity or organized tree vandalism in the district.
evidence: 4 illegal tree damage complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.8 weekly average (433% spike, z-score 4.91)
Concurrent spike in 'Overgrown Tree/Branches' complaints (15 last week vs 5.4 avg) suggests tree-maintenance crisis
647 building permits filed in last 90 days (71 new buildings, 441 alterations) may indicate construction-related tree damage
reporting_angles: Investigate whether active construction projects (247-56 90th Ave rezoning in public review; JFK Conduit Logistics demapping completed) are damaging street trees
Interview Parks Department about enforcement against illegal tree removal and identify specific streets affected

themes_detail.label: Asbestos and smoking complaints cluster
themes_detail.summary: Asbestos complaints surged to 3 last week versus a 0.4 per week baseline (700% spike, z-score 5.42), and smoking/vaping complaints hit 3 last week versus 0.5 baseline (500% spike, z-score 5.0)—suggesting potential indoor air quality crisis or problem building(s).
evidence: Asbestos: 3 complaints last week vs. 0.4 weekly average (700% spike, z-score 5.42)
Smoking/Vaping: 3 complaints last week vs. 0.5 weekly average (500% spike, z-score 5.0)
Two separate but coinciding spikes suggest possible single problematic building or development site affecting air quality
reporting_angles: Cross-reference asbestos and smoking complaints by address to identify whether they cluster at same location(s)

Contact Department of Buildings and Department of Environmental Protection to investigate whether renovation/demolition work (647 permits filed in 90 days) is releasing asbestos or creating smoking violations

themes_detail.label: Street conditions and infrastructure strain
themes_detail.summary: Street condition complaints remain the top category at 2,076 over 90 days, with concurrent spikes in overgrown tree/branches (179% increase to 15 last week) and illegal tree damage (433% this week), alongside 647 building permits filed—indicating infrastructure stress that community board budgets have repeatedly requested DOT address.
evidence: 2,076 street condition complaints over 90 days (largest complaint category overall)
Overgrown tree/branches: 15 last week vs. 5.4 average (179% spike, z-score 4.55)
Community Board has requested street reconstruction funding in every budget cycle—pattern indicates unresolved chronic problem
reporting_angles: Request DOT street repair and tree maintenance schedules to understand gaps between complaint volume and response capacity
Interview Parks Department and DOT on whether construction activity (647 permits) is straining street maintenance resources
